### macOS: now lives in the menu bar, and leaves the Dock

**On macOS the app will disappear from the Dock and from Command-Tab after this update.**
That is deliberate, not a fault.

It now sits in the **menu bar**, alongside the other things that stay running. Clicking the
icon gives you "Open DisplayMuxAuto" and "Quit DisplayMuxAuto".

**Windows is unaffected** — the system tray behaves exactly as before.

### Why

Closing the window on macOS did not quit the app. It hid the window and kept running, the
same as on Windows — except that the tray it was hiding into is Windows-only.

So the app went on running in the background with its Dock icon still there, nothing
answering a click on it, and nothing in the menu bar either. The only way back was launching
it again from Finder or Spotlight.

It now has its own menu bar icon, and stays out of the Dock entirely. This app does not need
to be interacted with in normal use — switching has a global shortcut
(`Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Space`) and a switcher window — and the main window is a place to set
things up, not something to switch to.

### Why the version jumps to 0.3.0

Nothing here breaks compatibility and nothing needs configuring, so the rule as written
called this 0.2.1.

But the rule had a gap: **where the app is, and how it is reached, changed**. A macOS user
who updates goes looking in the Dock and does not find it. A version number's job is to
signal before anyone reads the notes, and a patch number on a change like this stops it doing
that job.

A third clause now covers it, written down in `docs/versioning.md`.

### Known limitations

- The menu bar icon is a placeholder line glyph; the designed icon is still in progress.
- The contents of a reply are still unauthenticated, and the pairing password is used
  directly as the HMAC key with no KDF, minimum eight characters (see the v0.2.0 notes).
- Undoing a merge leaves the inputs and notes that merging folded into the display the other
  identity joined.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper
  may require manual approval.
